newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One asks for delay of Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Finance One asks for delay of Q1 results.

text.p: Finance One Plc , Thailand's largest finance firm, on Friday asked the Stock Exchange of Thailand for a delay in its release of first quarter earnings.
The company said it asked for the delay because of the complicated nature of its merger process with Thai Danu Bank Plc.
In separate statements, both Thai Danu and Finance One also asked the bourse to extend the suspension of their shares.
Shares of both companies were suspended in early March as talk began that the two companies were planning to link up in the largest ever merger of two financial institutions in Thailand.
The Bank of Thailand has since said the merger has become a takeover of cash-strapped Finance One by Thai Danu.
Finance One said it wanted to delay the release of its first quarter results -- originally due on Friday -- until the merger process was completed around May 23.

"We would like to inform you that due to the complicated nature of the merger process, the Board of Directors have to exercise their decisions with extreme prudence," Finance One said in a statement to the SET.
Thai Danu and Finance One both requested their share suspensions continue until the boards reach their decision around May 23.
On Thursday, officials from the two firms said top executives had postponed their board meeting to vote on the merger until May 23.
They said the companies needed more time to study all the documents and obtain more information.
Thai investors are awaiting details of the proposed joining of the two companies as it is a key element in the government's policy to bolster stability in the financial sector, analysts said.
The proposed deal, announced at the end of February, is said to have run into trouble in recent weeks over the valuations of the assets of Finance One.
